name: Heritage Speakers and Family Languages
title: Heritage Speakers and Family Languages
answer: Heritage speakers are students who already speak a language other than English at home, often fluently, but who may have had little practice reading and writing it. AI can generate reading and writing materials pitched at their real level, and family language stories can become social studies projects that honor family knowledge while building skills in both languages. The teacher and the student stay responsible for checking that the language variety and the translation are faithful.

crumbs.name: Social Studies, Civics, and World Languages

sections.body: Many students come to school already speaking a language other than English at home. These heritage speakers may understand and speak that language well but have had few chances to read and write it, so they do not fit neatly into beginner or advanced classes. AI can help teachers produce reading and writing materials at the right level for these students. The teacher still checks that the language in those materials matches the variety the student's family actually speaks. This solves the problem of materials that are either too easy or too hard, and of a student's home language being treated as a gap rather than a strength.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In world languages classes, teachers can use AI to draft reading and writing exercises tuned to heritage speakers rather than to true beginners or advanced second language learners, then verify the language against the variety the family uses. In social studies, a student can interview a grandparent about migration, work, or community life in the family's language, then translate and share the story with the class. AI transcription and translation can support that work, with the student checking and correcting the output. The project honors the family's knowledge and builds the student's skills in both languages. The text does not give separate grade band guidance, so these practices apply across the grade levels where heritage speakers are present.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or finding for this idea. It rests on practice rather than research, describing what teachers can do with heritage speakers and family language projects rather than citing measured results.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Teachers should be careful when translating family stories. Machine translation can miss tone, humor, and cultural meaning, and a family's story deserves care. Where possible, the student or a fluent speaker should review any translation before it is shared. The goal is to carry the family's voice faithfully, not to flatten it. The decisions about what is faithful and what gets shared stay with the student, the family, and the teacher, not with the tool.
